.ad-wrapper[data-astro-cid-fgwukgf6]{margin:2rem 0;text-align:center} Air Fryer Toolkit Convert Reverse Food presets Brands Chart Guide EN English Español Português Français Deutsch Time by size Same temperature, different time: thickness decides how long the heat takes to reach the middle. Size Air fryer Pack says Thin strips or chicken fingers 400°F / 205°C · 10 min 425°F / 220°C · 13 min Standard breaded tenders 400°F / 205°C · 12 min 425°F / 220°C · 15 min Thick or homestyle tenders 400°F / 205°C · 15 min 425°F / 220°C · 19 min The pack says raw, the coating says done Breaded tenders come in two kinds that look identical in the bag. Some are fully cooked and only need reheating. Many others, especially store brands and “homestyle” strips, are raw chicken in a pre-browned coating, and the pack says so in small print: uncooked, cook thoroughly, or raw. The coating on these was fried just long enough to set it, so it looks golden before the air fryer even starts, and it is easy to pull them when they look ready while the chicken inside is still raw. A tender is also thicker than a nugget, so the centre needs longer to come up to temperature. Treat every bag as raw unless it clearly says fully cooked, and use a thermometer on the fattest strip. Worked example: a bag of raw breaded tenders A bag of uncooked breaded tenders says 425°F for 15 minutes, turning once. In a basket air fryer that becomes 400°F for 12 minutes. Preheat 4 minutes, lay six to eight tenders flat without touching, and flip at 6 minutes. Thin chicken fingers take about 10 minutes; thick homestyle tenders need about 15. Probe the thickest one before serving; fully cooked tenders can come out a few minutes sooner. How to tell they are done For raw tenders, 165°F (74°C) in the thickest strip, measured with the probe pushed in from the end so the tip sits in the middle. The coating colour tells you nothing here, because it was browned before freezing. Fully cooked tenders only need to be hot all the way through. In both cases the crumb should be crisp on both sides with no soft patches where strips touched. Before they go in Find the cooking line on the pack before anything else and note whether it says raw or fully cooked. Do not thaw them. Leave a gap between strips, and give the coating a light spray of oil if it looks dry and floury. Wash your hands after handling raw breaded chicken, even frozen. About 12 minutes at 400°F, flipped at 6 minutes. Thin strips take about 10 minutes and thick ones about 15. How do I know if frozen tenders are raw? The pack tells you. Look for “uncooked”, “raw” or “cook thoroughly” near the instructions. If it is unclear, treat them as raw and check with a thermometer. What temperature should raw tenders reach? 165°F (74°C) in the thickest piece, measured with a thermometer, not judged by colour. How are tenders different from nuggets? Nuggets are almost always fully cooked and small. Tenders are thicker and often raw, so they need more time and a thermometer. Do I need to flip frozen tenders? Yes, once at 6 minutes, so the side against the basket crisps too.
